Title: Police raid workshops behind national gun-manufacturing ring in HCMC and Dong Nai
Location: HCMC
Description:
Police seized hundreds of finished and unfinished craft rifles when they dismantled a national arms-manufacturing and trafficking ring based in Ho Chi Minh City and Dong Nai on 7 June 2026. Acting on Telegram and Viber accounts flagged for large-scale gun-component trading, police first arrested ring leaders Nguyen Duc Hiep, Sam Van Thuyen, and Pham Van Tuan between late April and 6 May 2026, together with 6 further defendants across Lao Cai, Ninh Binh, Phu Tho, Hung Yen, and Ha Tinh, charging all 9 with illegal possession and sale of military weapons. That raid recovered 64-65 self-made gun bodies, 6 complete PCP air rifles, 8 additional air guns, 1 shotgun with 20 rounds of ammunition, up to 40 kilograms of lead pellets, 60 suppressors, and gun-manufacturing machinery including a press and a lathe.

Police later raided two machine shops disguised as ordinary civilian workshops on 7 June 2026, detaining 5 more suspects — Vu Manh Quyet (workshop owner), Nguyen Thi Quynh Nhu, Nguyen Cong Quy, Nguyen Cong Danh, and Truong Anh Tai. They seized 178 finished PCP gun bodies, 113 magazines, 300 aluminum alloy blanks, hundreds of additional unassembled components, 4 CNC milling machines, 1 CNC lathe, and 2 desktop computers.

Quyet told investigators he had run the workshop since 2023, filling thousands of orders for buyers domestically and abroad, and had machined roughly 200 gun bodies between February and May 2026 alone for a Viber contact known as "Ga Rung." Police also identified Tran Huu Trang (born 1997, Dong Nai) as the designer of the PCP gun-body models supplied to Hiep, describing the full network — from component design and manufacture through assembly to online sale — as the largest such operation uncovered to date.

Images of the raids showed hundreds of unassembled firearm components, including dozens of milled rifle receivers (bodies) at various stages of production. Images also showed workshop equipment, including several large CNC machines and lathes.
Weapons:
243 unfinished craft rifles
6 PCP air rifles (craft rifles)
8 additional air guns
1 shotgun
20 rounds of ammunition
dozens of kilograms of lead/lead pellets
additional unassembled components and manufacturing materials.
Actors: Criminal Organization (Nguyen Duc Hiep, born 1990; Sam Van Thuyen, born 1985; Pham Van Tuan, born 1990; Vu Manh Quyet, born 1987; Tran Huu Trang, born 1997; Nguyen Thi Quynh Nhu; Nguyen Cong Quy, born 1994; Nguyen Cong Danh; Truong Anh Tai; 9 total formally charged as of reporting); Police (Ha Tinh Provincial Police Cybersecurity and High-Tech Crime Prevention Department, Ha Tinh Provincial Security Investigation Agency, Ho Chi Minh City Police, Dong Nai Police).

Title: HCMC police dismantle 3D printing manufacturing ring spanning multiple provinces
Location: Tan Son Nhi Ward, HCMC
Description:
Police seized at least 30 firearms, 9 partially assembled firearms, roughly 100 gun components in production, one hand grenade, and over 1,000 rounds of ammunition and arrested 34 suspects when they dismantled a manufacturing and online-sales ring led by Nguyen Ngoc Son across Ho Chi Minh City, Tay Ninh, Dong Thap, and Vinh Long between 30 May and 11 July 2026.

Son, who began building homemade pistols from online-ordered parts in January 2026 and sold them via anonymized Facebook accounts for around VND 5 million each, recruited associates with metalworking skills to mass-produce components and shipped completed weapons disguised inside computer-tower boxes via intercity couriers; buyers paid into bank accounts registered to other people to obscure the money trail. The investigation also uncovered links to drug distribution, leading to seven additional arrests for drug sales and organizing drug use.

14 3D-printed pistols (craft handguns)
7 ZP-5 converted revolvers (craft handguns)
7 converted pistols (craft handguns)
2 3D-printed MP5-style submachine guns (craft submachine guns)

Actors: Criminal Organization (Nguyen Ngoc Son, born 1993 — leader, charged; more than 30 associates, 34 total defendants charged as of 11 July 2026); Police (Ho Chi Minh City Police Criminal Police Department).

Title: Nationwide PCP air-rifle manufacturing ring dismantled from Bac Ninh base
Location: Lam Thao Commune, Bac Ninh
Description:
Police arrested 33 suspects and seized 58 guns (53 PCP air rifles, 2 pellet/shotgun-type guns, and 1 birdshot gun), roughly 130,000 lead pellets, thousands of gun components, and manufacturing machinery — including a metal lathe, hydraulic presses, air compressors, a grinder, a metal cutter, and drill presses — in a nationwide raid on a firearms-manufacturing ring led by Ngo Quang Vy of Lam Thao Commune, Bac Ninh, on 13 September 2025.

Investigators said Vy, a trained mechanical engineer, began buying air guns, lead pellets, and components from foreign websites in 2019, then used workshop machinery to modify and reassemble the components to increase the weapons' lethality before reselling them online; the ring rented two houses in Hai Duong as a warehouse and workshop, sold through YouTube, Facebook, Telegram, Viber, and Zalo livestreams, and had completed roughly 3,500 orders nationwide in early 2025 alone worth tens of billions of dong, with many buyers in mountainous regions seeking hunting guns.

Twenty-six suspects — including Vy, relative and warehouse manager Ngo Van Trong, Nguyen Thanh Do (born 1994), Ngo Van Huynh (born 1992), Nguyen Dinh Dong (born 1994), Tran Van Thai (born 1992), and Nguyen Manh Linh (born 1988) — were formally charged with illegally manufacturing, trading, and possessing military weapons. Police said the operation, tracked for over a year, was the largest of its kind uncovered to date, and noted that under a weapons law effective 1 January 2025, gas- and air-powered guns and their components are classified as military weapons. During the searches, police said residents voluntarily surrendered 10 further guns of the same type after outreach on the dangers of illegal weapons.
Weapons: 68 craft rifles; thousands of gun components and manufacturing machinery.
Actors: Criminal Organization (Ngo Quang Vy, born 1992; Ngo Van Trong; Nguyen Thanh Do, born 1994; Ngo Van Huynh, born 1992; Nguyen Dinh Dong, born 1994; Tran Van Thai, born 1992; Nguyen Manh Linh, born 1988; 19 further charged suspects); Police (Ministry of Public Security Criminal Police Department, Lai Chau Provincial Police, Ha Tinh Provincial Police, Bac Ninh Provincial Police, Hai Phong Police); Civilian Community (residents who voluntarily surrendered 10 additional guns during the operation).

Title: Police Dismantle Transnational Arms Trafficking Ring Selling Over 1,000 Converted Toy Guns in Ninh Binh
Location: Yen Khanh, Ninh Binh
Description:
Ha Tĩnh Provincial Police dismantled a major transnational arms trafficking ring in late 2024, seizing 532 firearms, nearly 37,000 rounds of ammunition, 211 grams of drugs, and two grenades. The investigation led to the arrest of 45 individuals across 15 provinces—including Hà Nội, Hồ Chí Minh City, Bình Dương, Tây Ninh, and Ninh Bình—with 43 formally charged for trafficking, manufacturing, storing, and illegally using military-grade weapons and for drug offenses. Authorities estimate the network sold over 1,000 firearms both within Vietnam and internationally, including to buyers in Laos and Cambodia. The criminal operation was highly organized, using social media platforms like Facebook, Zalo, and YouTube to advertise and sell weapons sourced from China, Laos, and Cambodia. The suspects "maintained ties with international arms suppliers," and imported parts from abroad in order "to complete the weapons" (suggesting firearm conversion).

According to Tuoi Tre, the arms dealers advertised and facilitated illegal transactions through fake social media profiles, providing non-registered phone numbers for potential buyers to make contact. Buyers could easily select the type of weapon they wanted, provide their details or reach out directly via phone or virtual nicknames, and transfer money to the seller. Once an order was placed, the traffickers would disassemble the weapons, pack the parts into multiple parcels, and ship them through various channels, including express delivery services, motorbike couriers, passenger vehicles, and trains. URL: 

VNExpress reported that the focus of the operation took place in Yen Khanh, Ninh Binh Province. The chief suspect, Vu Anh Tu, imported many types of toy guns from abroad, changed the internal components (such as reinforcing the gun barrel and adding a firing pin), then applied a new layer of paint. A toy gun cost 200,000 VND to buy, and 400,000 VND for accessories. After being "modified", it is sold for the lowest price of 5 million VND, and the average price is 10-15 million VND. If the customer wants to assemble it, Tu and his juniors will import expensive components to do it according to instructions, earning 70-80 million VND, some guns cost more than 100 million VND. Vu relied on six lieutenants to collect the profits from the sales, which was paid out to dozens of affiliates in monthly salaries ranging between VND 5-7 million.The suspects communicated using fake social media accounts or junk SIM cards, and never met in person; they coordinated via a private chat group, and paying their salaries via bank cards. Customers provided their contact information, transfer money via bank account or ship COD (receive goods, check and then pay the delivery staff). The suspects "had close ties with suspects in arms trafficking in Cambodia and Laos." 

Images showed hundreds of rifles (possibly toy/airsoft), dozens of Chinese ZP-5 toy revolvers, AR- and AK-pattern assault rifles (ARP9 airsoft), ammunition, pen guns, high-quality gas rifles, a shotgun, a Glock pistol.

~480 converted toy revolvers/pen guns (craft handguns; approximate)
~48 rifles/airsoft rifles/gas rifles (craft rifles; approximate)
1 shotgun 
1 Glock pistol

37,000 rounds of ammunition

Title: Police Seize AK-Pattern Rifles and Pistols From Criminal Kingpin's Kidnapping Plot in Ho Chi Minh City
Location: Diamond Islands, Binh Trung Tay, Thu Duc City, HCMC
Description:
Police seized 11 firearms and over 1,400 rounds of ammunition when they arrested 16 individuals suspected of various crimes, including the illegal manufacture, purchase, sale, transportation and storage of military weapon, fraud, property appropriation, and gambling.

VNExpress reported that the seizure was part of a high profile operation to arrest a notorious criminal kingpin, Pham Duc Binh (alias Binh Kiem), who intended to orchestrate the kidnapping of "famous models and singers" and force them to commit recorded sexual acts, which would then be sent to affiliates in the United States and put on pornography websites for monetization. To do so, he attempted to organize the purchase of several firearms, including AK-pattern rifles, and ammunition abroad and smuggle them into Vietnam. Binh Kiem, a former soldier, previously served a long sentence for kidnapping a businessman in 2005. 

VNExpress further reported that Binh Kiem employed an associate, Nguyen Tuan An, to procure weapons in Laos and bring them back to Vietnam. Laotian police arrested An in Laos with the firearms. In total, police seized three AK-pattern assault rifles, eight pistols, over 1,400 rounds of ammunition, five magazines, five bulletproof vests, and drugs. Images showed one Beretta M92 pistol, one Type 56-1 assault rifle, one AKMS assault rifle, and ammunition.

An additional VNExpress report said that Binh Kiem ordered his associates to seek out firearms in early July 2024, particularly firearms of "Western European" origin. In one instance, he associates were defrauded by an individual claiming to possess an AK rifle, soliciting VND 18 million VND for the rifle, VND 6 million for two magazines, and VND 3.3 million for 100 rounds of ammunition from the suspects. The individual made off with the payment to payoff personal debts and expenses. The transaction took place over Zalo messenger. 

Additional reporting provided more details about Binh and the scheme. Binh (55, from Quang Ninh) earned the nickname "Kiem" from a stint in an HCMC military police battalion; before 1991 he used his position as a soldier to steal and trade unit weapons. After discharge he led a gang running protection rackets, loan-sharking, and gambling dens in Ho Chi Minh City, at one point rivaling mob boss Truong Van Cam. His record includes a 1996 escape from a labor camp, further gambling and assault convictions through the 2000s, and a 2004 kidnapping of Tram Trong Ngan, son of businessman Tram Be, for a $10 million ransom, using an AK rifle, five handguns, over 400 rounds, and two grenades — for which he was ultimately sentenced to 30 years. 

He completed that sentence and was released on April 7, 2024, after which the Ministry of Public Security's Criminal Police Department (C02) placed him under surveillance; he and his associates regularly gathered at a luxury apartment on Kim Cuong (Diamond) Island in Thu Duc City. Described as paranoid and trusting almost no one, he avoided drugs, alcohol, and gambling, and was said to be fixated specifically on high-lethality Western European military firearms. To build a public image he had associates fund events, shows, and charity work; he reportedly conceived the kidnapping-extortion scheme while still in prison, planning to force each victim to produce 12 fifteen-minute episodes (one released monthly) for paid distribution on adult websites, and to have a lawyer draft consent paperwork to cover himself legally.

The weapons case prosecutors ultimately charged as three separate arms trafficking incidents between April and October 2024. In the Laos deal, Nguyen Tuan An (42) bought one AK rifle, four magazines, 250 rounds of 9mm ammunition, and 242 rounds of AK ammunition for VND 227 million. Lao authorities separately arrested and charged the Laos-based seller, identified as Lao-Vietnamese national Somsak Thanuvong, along with other buyers who had purchased weapons from him. 

Separately, in early July 2024 an old prison contact, Nam Phuong (55), introduced Binh to Huynh Hoang Vu (53, alias "Vu Meo"), who gave Binh a Beretta pistol and 13 rounds as a gift at a goat hot-pot restaurant owned by Chu Van Hoang Anh (35). Binh had Hoang Anh hide the weapon, which Hoang Anh eventually buried in his father's garden in Lam Dong province, where investigators recovered it on October 30, 2024. 

A third case involved Binh asking Tran Dinh Thien to source a weapon. Thien enlisted Le Minh Nghia, who instead defrauded Thien of at least 21.3 million VND over Zalo without delivering a weapon.
Weapons:
3 AK-pattern assault rifles (Type 56-1, AKMS)
1 shotgun
8 pistols (incl. one Beretta M92, one TT pistol, and one revolver)
1,400+ rounds of ammunition
5 magazines and 5 bulletproof vests (not tallied)
Actors: Criminal organization (led by former soldier 'Binh Kiem'); Former police/soldier (ringleader); Police

A separate revolver bought online in 2021 by Tran Van Thanh Toan — unconnected to Triet's manufacturing — was also seized after Toan brought it to Triet for repair days before the raid. Title: Police Seize Pistol, Shotgun, and Grenades From Arms Trafficking Network in Lao Cai
Location: Tan An, Van Ban, Lao Cai
Description:
Police seized "1 military gun, 1 hunting gun, 1 ammunition box, 5 grenades," 83 rounds of assorted ammunition, and a large amount of bullet casings and pellets when they arrested four members of a suspected arms trafficking network. Police discovered the network through online monitoring of a Facebook page that claimed to sell weapons. The main suspect, Sam Van Cong, confessed to having bought and sold numerous weapons over social media.

Images showed one M1911A1 pistol, one hunting shotgun, three F-1 hand grenades (possibly inert), two M67-like grenades (possibly inert), and thousands of rounds of ammunition and shell casings.

Cong An HCMC reported that police first detected the Facebook page in early March 2024 and eventually linked it to Suspect Cong, who posted from fake accounts. The suspect confessed to purchasing items to manufacture ammunition from individuals through Facebook and Telegram since October 2023. He produced 200 rubber bullets and 150 metal bullets. He bought the pistol from someone he met online.

The remaining suspects were linked to the M1911A1 pistol. Suspect Cong purchased the gun through Pham Hien Vinh of Soc Trang so that he could use it to generate user engagement on social media. He paid Vinh VND 40 million for the weapon. Vinh did not directly own the pistol; in September 2023, he met Dao Khuong Cuoc, who claimed to have inherited a Type 54 pistol from his father. Vinh, who was interested in collecting the pistol, offered to buy it but realized upon inspection that the pistol was an M1911A1, and so the sale failed. Vinh later contacted a separate suspect, who offered to buy the gun for VND 25 million (of which Vinh offered VND 13 million to Cuoc). The suspect seeking the gun transferred VND 2 million to secure the order. Nevertheless, Vinh ended up selling the gun to Cong. After receiving Cong's payment, Vinh purchased the gun from Cuoc. Vinh then disassembled the weapon and sent it to Cong by post. URL: https://congan.com.vn/vu-an/triet-pha-duong-day-mua-ban-trai-phep-vu-khi-quan-dung-qua-mang_164509.html

1 M1911A1 pistol

Title: Police Seize 230 Firearms Smuggled From Thailand and Cambodia in Ho Chi Minh City
Location: District 8, HCMC
Description:
Police seized 230 firearms, 4,750 rounds of ammunition, two ammunition machines, 10 bags of ammunition, and 54 ammunition packages when they arrested two suspects who smuggled guns from Thailand and Cambodia and sold them online (the guns may have been airsoft weapons). The main suspect, who had a prior record for "possession of dangerous toys," allegedly began operating in early 2023 and made VND 300 million (USD 12,016). 

Investigators traced the operation to a Facebook account, Telegram channel, website (baodenairsoft.com), and YouTube channel all branded "báo đen airsoft" ("black panther airsoft"). Listings ran 20–40 million VND (roughly USD 800–1,600) per weapon. The group communicated with buyers only by phone, Zalo, Facebook, or Telegram rather than meeting in person. Buyers paid a deposit by bank transfer upfront with the balance paid via bank transfer on receipt through delivery apps; Thai frequently changed his residence and storage locations to evade tracking, and the group would halt transactions immediately if they suspected police attention.

Title: Police Seize 92 Firearms From Online Arms Trafficker in Quang Ngai
Location: Dam Thuy Bac, Duc Minh, Mo Duc, Quang Ngai
Description:
Police seized 92 guns of various types (including military guns, hunting guns and dangerous toys) along with more than 14,600 sports bullets (presumably pellets) and support tools when they arrested a suspected online arms trafficker. Police discovered the seller through "online scanning" in 2023. Police arrested the suspect as he transported weapons and ammunition following a long period of surveillance. Police seized the weapons after searching his residence.

The suspect confessed to ordering the items from within and outside of Vietnam and were shipped to Quang Ngai via post. The suspect "hid them in a secret warehouse and continuously changed the location of the warehouse to avoid detection." He advertised and sold the weapons on closed Facebook groups and YouTube channels, claiming to have made hundreds of transactions. The suspect said customers communicate over Zalo and Telegram, often paying in advance into a back account without the seller's name. The suspect shipped with goods disassembled in staggered packages via freight forwarding services. 

A police official said traffickers often use junk SIM/phone numbers to communicate and that social media interactions are often cross-border. Images and video of the seized weapons showed dozens of revolvers, various airsoft pistols (including AAP-01, Glock 18C, Baretta M92 variants), one shotgun, and one US-origin CZ 457 rifle.

~90 revolvers/airsoft pistols, likely converted (craft handguns)
1 shotgun

~14,600 pellets (not counted as live ammunition)

Title: Police seize military-grade and sporting firearms from drug-trafficking ring in Ho Chi Minh City
Location: Binh Thanh District, HCMC
Description:

Description:

Title: Four friends convicted after borrowing and test-firing online-purchased revolver in An Giang
Location: Vong Dong Commune, Thoai Son District, An Giang
Description:
Police seized one converted revolver and two rounds of ammunition along with 7.8376 grams of methamphetamine when they searched Bui Thi Nhung’s home in Vong Dong Commune, Thoai Son District, An Giang on 23 October 2023. Investigation revealed that Ho Van Tuan bought the revolver in September 2023 and lent it to friends to test-fire before pawning it, leading to the conviction of four suspects.

In September 2023, Tuan bought the revolver and six rounds via Facebook for VND 4 million, having a friend transfer payment on his behalf; he lost one round upon receiving the weapon and hid it at home. On 14 October, Luu Huynh Ty and Tran Thanh Binh borrowed the gun from Tuan for a VND 30,000 fee. They took it to a vacant lot in Ap Tan Hiep, Vong The Commune, where Ty fired one round while Binh filmed on his phone.

Ty returned the gun the next day but, after enjoying the experience, borrowed it again two days later and fired two more rounds at the same location with other friends present. Ty returned the gun to Tuan on 22 October; short of cash, Tuan pawned it that evening to Le Thanh Tan for VND 200,000, and Tan hid it inside a broken electric kettle at the home of his partner, Bui Thi Nhung.

Police searched Nhung's home following a tip and recovered the revolver. Nhung and Tan were detained on drug charges, and Ty turned himself in the same day. Forensic examination determined the smooth-bore revolver, firing 5.6x15.5mm ammunition, could cause injury or death and qualified as a military-grade weapon. On 27 March 2024, the An Giang Provincial People's Court sentenced Tuan to 2 years, Ty to 1 year 3 months, and Tan to 1 year 3 months for illegal possession and trading of a military-grade weapon, and gave Binh a 1-year suspended sentence for illegal transport of the weapon.

Title: Nationwide air-rifle manufacturing and sales ring traced to Hanoi trafficker
Location: Thanh Cao Commune, Thanh Oai District, Hanoi
Description:
Police seized 4 assembled air rifles, 290 rounds of sporting ammunition, 11kg of lead pellets, and hundreds of unassembled gun components when they arrested Nguyen Van Vu at his home in Thanh Cao Commune, Thanh Oai District, Hanoi on 29 August 2023. The arrest stemmed from a March 2023 case in Pleiku, Gia Lai, in which police seized a military-pattern gun, an air-powered gun, and a hunting gun from Tran Quoc Khuong, who told investigators he had bought a hunting gun and 16 rounds from a seller on Zalo; tracing that seller led investigators to Vu over several months, and from Vu to three further Hanoi-area suspects — Vu Van Hai, Nguyen Van Trieu, and Nguyen Trung Ban — arrested by 3 September 2023 with 3 more assembled guns, 18 rounds, and 625 additional components.

The wider investigation ultimately charged 37 defendants across 15 provinces, identifying Hai and Ban as ring leaders who commissioned machine shops in Hanoi and Bac Giang to manufacture gun components, which core members assembled and sold via Zalo, Facebook, and YouTube, shipping components split across multiple parcels and couriers to avoid detection. Images of several rifles showed production patterns consisted with CNC machining.

The final court tally recorded 33 firearms legally classified as military-pattern weapons and 5 additional air/sporting guns (38 functional firearms, plus 7 recovered non-functional guns), 832 rounds of sporting ammunition, 969 rounds and 11kg of additional lead pellets, and 1,974 unassembled components; in September 2025 the Gia Lai court sentenced Hai to 14 years, Ban to 10 years, Vu to 12 years 6 months, and Trieu to 12 years, with the remaining defendants — mostly buyers who purchased complete or component guns for hunting — receiving sentences from 15 months to 8 years.
Weapons:
38 craft rifles, 7 unspecified firearms
1,801 rounds of ammunition
1,974 unassembled gun components.

Title: Authorities seize arms cache following insurgent attack in Dak Lak Province
Location: Ea Tieu and Ea Ktur communes, Cu Kuin District, Dak Lak Province
Description:
An armed group described by Vietnamese authorities as an insurgent movement (self-styled “linh Dega” or “Dega soldiers” and apparently linked to the exiled FULRO organization) attacked the headquarters of the Ea Tieu and Ea Ktur Commune People's Committees using firearms (including craft weapons, air guns, and sporting guns), grenades, knives, and Molotov cocktails in Cu Kuin District, Dak Lak Province on 11 June 2023. Insurgents killed nine people, wounded at least two police officers, and took three civilians hostage.

At the Ea Tieu commune office, a group of roughly 10 attackers stormed and set fire to the building, killing two on-duty commune police officers before shooting dead the commune chairman as they withdrew. At the Ea Ktur commune office, a larger group of roughly 30 attackers forced a truck driver to block the access road with his vehicle and killed him, then stormed the office, killing two police officers, wounding two others, killing the commune party secretary and two civilians, and taking three ethnic-minority residents hostage.

Police and army units launched an immediate manhunt across Cu Kuin District and the wider Central Highlands, arresting suspects in stages -- 39 by the morning of 13 June, 45 by that evening, 74 by 20 June -- while progressively recovering weapons used in the attack. The reported cache included 23 firearms (a mix of military-issue weapons, craft firearms, and air guns), 2 grenades, 1,199 rounds of ammunition, 15 detonators, and approximately 1.2 kg of explosive material. Police rescued two of the three hostages directly, while the third freed himself. The alleged ringleader, Y Tho Ayun (alias Ama Kzruh), was captured around 15-16 June. All fugitives had been captured by 21 July.

Vietnamese authorities alleged the attack was organized and directed by FULRO-linked individuals based in the United States, who recruited and incited domestic participants online. Sources name the overseas figures as Y Mut Mlo, Y Cik Nie, Y Nien Eya, Y But Eban, Y Chang Bya, and either Y Sol Nie or Y Quynh Bdap. In January 2024, the Dak Lak Provincial People's Court tried 100 defendants on charges including terrorism against the people's government, terrorism, organizing/brokering illegal exit from Vietnam, and concealing a crime; the six overseas-based defendants were tried and sentenced in absentia.

Title: Military court convicts 25 members of ammunition diversion ring in HCMC and Dong Nai
Location: Military Zone 7 Military Court, Duc Nhuan, HCMC
Description:
The Military Zone 7 Military Court sentenced 25 defendants, including 21 former servicemen, on 27 April 2023 for trafficking a total of 29,471 rounds of military ammunition diverted from Vietnamese army units between 2017 and 2021. Le Cong Luc, a finance officer with the Tan Phu District Military Command in Dong Nai, used contacts in the Ho Chi Minh City Military Command's ordnance branch to source 5.56mm and 7.62mm military ammunition.

He initially sold ammunition to Nguyen Cong Phi (a farmer seeking ammunition for hunting who he had become acquainted with while serving in Vinh Cuu District in 2012) as well as Dao Bich Son (a Facebook acquaintance seeking to resell ammunition). Luc sourced the ammunition under the pretense of organizing live-fire exercises from active servicemen, some of whom diverted stock from their own units' training and combat-readiness allocations while others sold ammunition they had themselves obtained from other servicemen.

Luc made 25 separate purchases from 2017-2021, totaling 23,221 5.56mm rounds and 6,250 7.62mm rounds for VND 261.3 million, then resold the ammunition on to Phi, Son, and other buyers repeatedly. The court sentenced Nguyen Trong Luc to 13 years for embezzlement of military weapons and illegal possession and trading of military weapons, and Le Cong Luc to 14 years for illegal trading of military weapons; the remaining 23 defendants received sentences ranging from 1 year 6 months to 11 years 6 months, with two receiving suspended sentences, and all were ordered to pay restitution to the affected military units.

Title: Police Dismantle Arms Manufacturing Network Selling Firearms Assembled From Online-Ordered Parts in Dong Nai
Location: Quarter 12, An Binh Ward, Bien Hoa City, Dong Nai
Description:
Police seized 14 firearms and more than 420 rounds of assorted ammunition when they arrested four members of a suspected arms trafficking ring on 17 March 2023. Police initially seized three guns (including a craft firearm, a shotgun and a K59 pistol), and around 300 rounds of ammunition from the residence of Hoang Viet Toi, the suspected network leader, in Ward 12, An Binh Commune, Bien Hoa City, Dong Nai before expanding their investigation to seize the remaining weapons and arrest the remaining suspects. 

A simultaneous raid of the residences of Nguyen Quang Cuong and Bui Vu Nhat Huy in An Binh Commune and Binh Da Commune, Bien Hoa City, led to the seizure of another 11 firearms, including a K59 pistol, 1 rubber bullet gun, 9 pellet guns, 9 rounds of ammunition, gun components, as well as 26 ecstasy pills.

The network was apparently led by Hoang Viet Toi who recently finished a prison sentence and had criminal connections. He linked up with some acquaintances who guided him to online market for buying and selling guns, ammunition, and parts and components. He decided to order gun parts and taught himself online how to assemble, modify, and repair firearms. He eventually assembled them into functioning firearms, and sought out teenage customers online based on advise from his acquaintances. He eventually befriended youth gangs and sold them firearms; some of which were seized by police responding to gang violence in late 2022 and 2023.

Cuong and Huy both learned how to assemble guns online, and sold weapons over social media for VND 10-15 million apiece. Huy would place special ammunition orders online for buyers on request, and used couriers to deliver the products. 

Cuong confessed that he was associated with gangs since a young age and was familiar with firearms due to this exposure. He began assembling and selling guns and ammunition online when he learned that criminal groups involved in debt collection, protection rackets, loan sharking, and other types of crime in Dong Nai province and surrounding areas were "hungry" for guns. Cuong sold his products for a higher price with the guarantee that he would immediately repair them if problems arose. Cuong produced his own ammunition. Cuong also made custom modifications to firearms to alter their noise profile. Cuong reportedly sold dozens of fiearms to criminal groups by the time of his arrest, and was planning on assembling dozens more. 

Images showed one ZP-5 revolver, one Ekol P29 pistol, one sawn-off shotgun, one air rifle, and dozens of rounds of assorted ammunition. An image posted by VietnamNet showed 5 additional shotguns, two possible air rifles, and three additional pistols.

Chua had bought the revolver and six rounds online through a Facebook contact for VND 2.5 million in October 2022. On 30 December, Chau Rone and Danh The Tan, recalling an earlier grievance involving Duong Van Loc, went to Chua's home looking for Loc; when Chua said Loc was not there, the two sides argued and Tan and Rone struck Chua before leaving. Angered, Chua walked to Rone's home with the revolver, fired a shot into the air, and then fired a second shot that struck Tan in the collarbone when Tan and Rone rushed him with plastic chairs. Chua turned himself in the next day.
Weapons: 1 converted revolver (craft handgun)

Title: Police Seize Converted Revolvers and Air Rifles From Firearm Repair Operation in An Giang
Location: Nui Sap, Thoai Son, An Giang
Description:
Police seized five firearms (two of which are considered 'military weapons'), four bullets, and four kilograms of pellets when they arrested a man suspected of buying and selling weapons online. Between January and June 2021, the suspect ordered three guns online for VND 6.2 million, assembled them, and hid them in his rented room. In Decmeber 2022, he was hired to repair two damaged ZP-5 converted revolvers. Using online instructions, he reassembled components from both weapons into one functional weapon. Images showed three high-end air rifles (apparently of Japanese origin).

Dai Bieu Nhan Dan posted additional images of the seized weapons, showing both ZP-5 revolvers (one is disassembled) as well as his equipment for manufacturing/repairing/modifying weapons.
Weapons:
2 converted 'ZP-5' revolvers (craft handguns)
3 air rifles (craft rifles)
4 rounds of ammunition
Actors: Criminal individual (manufacturer/repairer); Police

Title: Police seize gun-manufacturing workshop with seven firearms in Quang Nam
Location: Dien An Ward, Dien Ban Town, Quang Nam
Description: Police seized seven firearms, 1,015 rounds of assorted ammunition, and gun components from Le Hong Thai's home after identifying him as a manufacturer and seller of illegal weapons in Dien An Ward, Dien Ban Town, Quang Nam on 20 December 2022. Thai admitted sourcing gun parts and components through Zalo and Facebook groups, assembling complete firearms at home, and selling 21 guns to buyers in the area for VND 6-10 million each. Police subsequently summoned 12 identified buyers for questioning and recovered four more guns from them.

assorted gun components and parts

Title: Police seize two guns from fugitive drug trafficker in Son La manhunt
Location: Lung Xa Hamlet, Long Luong Commune, Van Ho District, Son La
Description:
Police seized one QBZ-95B assault rifle, one bolt action rifle, and 27 rounds of ammunition from wanted drug-trafficking fugitive Trang A Lau when 45 officers raided his hideout in Lung Xa Hamlet, Long Luong Commune, Van Ho District, Son La on 18 December 2022. Lau, brother of notorious drug kingpin Trang A Tang ("Tang Keangnam"), had been wanted since 2011 on drug-trafficking charges. Police tracked his movements before carrying out the raid.

Tang, sentenced to death in 2016 for trafficking nearly 1,800 heroin bricks between 2009 and his arrest, was a well-known figure in northern Vietnam's drug trade. Several of his associates in that earlier case also received death or life sentences.

27 rounds of ammunition

Title: Two firearms seized from Laos-Vietnam methamphetamine ring leader in Ha Nam
Location: Thanh Chau Ward, Phu Ly City, Ha Nam
Description:
Police seized two firearms and 29 rounds of ammunition tied to members of a Laos-Vietnam drug-trafficking ring led by Nguyen Van San and Lao national Xia Xiong in Chau Son Ward, Phu Ly City, Ha Nam Province on 16 December 2022. Police caught Sang and three Lao nationals -- Xia Xiong, Toua Xiong, and Chua Xong -- selling drugs and seized six bags of assorted drugs. An expanded investigation led to the emergency detention of Hanoi-based buyers Nguyen Tuan Anh and Hoang Phuong Thao on 18 December, a further drug seizure from Tuan Anh's home, and the identification of Hoang Thi Khanh Ly as another supplier.

Investigators determined Xia Xiong sourced methamphetamine, ketamine, heroin, and MDMA in Laos, had Toua Xiong smuggle it into Vietnam via the Cau Treo border crossing in Ha Tinh, and had Chua Xong deliver it to Sang in Ha Nam, who resold it to Tuan Anh and Thao in Hanoi. From September to December 2022, the ring trafficked a combined 23.6 kilograms of drugs. On 21-22 August 2024 the Ha Nam Provincial People's Court sentenced Sang, Xia Xiong, and Tuan Anh to death for drug trafficking, with Sang receiving an additional two-year sentence for illegal possession of a military-grade weapon to run alongside his death sentence; Toua Xiong, Chua Xong, Thao, and Ly received life sentences for drug trafficking.
Weapons:
2 unspecified firearms
29 rounds of ammunition

Title: Out-of-province trafficker caught with converted ZP-5 revolvers in Tay Ninh
Location: Gia Loc Ward, Trang Bang Town, Tay Ninh
Description: Police seized two converted ZP-5 revolvers and 12 rounds of ammunition from Ngo Hoang Khang when they caught him transporting the weapons by motorbike in Gia Loc Ward, Trang Bang Town, Tay Ninh on 4 December 2022. A search of his rented room in An Hoa Ward recovered further spent casings, gun components, and manufacturing tools. Khang, who had rented the room about a month earlier to evade detection, told police he had bought the guns and ammunition from an unidentified seller on social media, then assembled and sold weapons locally in Tay Ninh.
Weapons:

12 rounds of ammunition.

Title: Online arms dealer caught with three revolvers in Tay Ninh
Location: Tan Hung Commune, Tan Chau District, Tay Ninh
Description: Police seized a revolver and 5 rounds of ammunition from Le Huu Bang when they caught him selling the weapon to another buyer at Hiep Truong Market, Hoa Thanh Town, Tay Ninh on 15 November 2022. A follow-up search of his home in Tan Hung Commune, Tan Chau District recovered two further revolvers and 9 rounds. Bang told police that about a month earlier he had begun ordering weapons, ammunition, and knives through a Facebook account, then used online tutorials to modify and upgrade the items before reselling them on Facebook for a profit of VND 5–10 million per item, roughly double his purchase cost of VND 2–3 million.
Weapons:
3 converted revolvers (craft handguns)
14 rounds of ammunition.

Title: Man assembling revolvers and PCP air guns from online parts arrested in Binh Duong
Location: Thoi Hoa Ward, Ben Cat Town, Binh Duong
Description: Police seized a revolver and 10 rounds of ammunition when they arrested Ngo Quoc Cuong in Thoi Hoa Ward, Ben Cat Town, Binh Duong on 12 November 2022. The suspect was carrying the weapons to sell to a buyer. Police found a second revolver with 43 rounds, three PCP air guns, a pen gun, and numerous gun-assembly components — springs, barrels, stocks, suppressors, and air chambers — at his rented room. Cuong admitted ordering guns and parts online to assemble and resell for profit.
Weapons: 2 converted revolvers (craft handguns); 53 rounds of ammunition; 3 PCP air guns (craft rifles); 1 pen gun (craft handgun); assorted gun-assembly components.
Actors: Criminal Individual (Ngo Quoc Cuong, born 1987); Police (Ben Cat Town Police, Binh Duong).

Title: Craft firearm changes hands through resale chain uncovered in Tra Vinh
Location: Tan Phu Ward, District 7, HCMC
Description: Police arrested Bui Thanh Tha in Tan Phu Ward, District 7, Ho Chi Minh City on 10 November 2022 after he fled Tra Vinh, where he was charged with orchestrating the sale of a craft firearm and 5 rounds of ammunition that changed hands between Nguyen Trong Tinh, Tran Huu Thang, and Le Van Giang for between VND 3.5 and 5 million from January to May 2022. Thang had bought the gun to shoot a neighbor's dog.

Title: Three convicted over craft revolver sold to methamphetamine dealer in An Giang
Location: Nui To Commune, Tri Ton District, An Giang
Description:
Police seized a converted revolver and six rounds of ammunition from methamphetamine dealer Chau Soc Phol, who tried to sell the weapon alongside a drug delivery, in Tri Ton District, An Giang on 4 November 2022. Two co-defendants were later convicted over the sale.

In late September 2022, Nguyen Cong Thuan, buying methamphetamine from Phol, offered to sell him a ZM05 converted revolver for VND 8.5 million. Thuan recruited Lam Thanh Nguyen to help deliver the weapon to Phol's home two days later, and Nguyen was paid in methamphetamine for his help. Phol test-fired the revolver twice without it discharging before storing it at home.

On 4 November 2022, Phol arranged to sell 200 doses of methamphetamine to a buyer using the Zalo handle "Sang Gia," who asked Phol to bring the revolver along to view; Tri Ton District Police intercepted Phol at Ap To Ha, Nui To Commune while he was en route with roughly 29.92 grams of methamphetamine and the revolver, and arrested him. Forensic examination determined the revolver was a handcrafted, smooth-bore weapon capable of firing live rounds and causing injury or death, while the six accompanying rounds were sport-type, not military-grade. Phol was separately convicted and sentenced to 12 years for the drug sale on 31 July 2023; on the weapons charge, the Provincial People's Court sentenced Phol to 2.5 years, Thuan to 1 year 9 months, and Nguyen to 5 years.

6 rounds of ammunition

Title: Forest Ranger Injured by Air Gun Pellet During Land Dispute Confrontation in Lam Dong
Location: Phu Hoi, Duc Trong, Lam Dong

Title: Gun and ammunition seized alongside drugs in Binh Duong

Title: Police Seize 400 Toy Guns Intended for Conversion in Rach Gia
Location: Rach Gia, Kien Giang
Description:
Report highlighting the increasing proliferation of converted firearms, homemade firearms, and online sales. Highlights a major seizure in Rach Gia, Kien Giang Province in October 2022 in which police seized 400 toy guns that a suspect intended to convert into firearms, who said was a relatively easy process. Police in Kien Giang and An Giang provinces say there have been dozens of cases involving converted/homemade firearms since 2022. Report highlights several other cases:
- Two men used a plastic gun to rob a bank in Ha Tien City, Kien Giang Province.
- 42 suspects used homemade guns in land disputes in Phu Quoc, Kien Giang Province.
- A 17-year-old boy bought a homemade gun for VND 700,000 (USD 28) and shot and injured someone in Long Xuyen City, An Giang Province.
- Police recovered "rubber bullets" after shots were fired during an altercation at a restaurant in Nguyen Minh Duong Street, Dao Thanh, My Tho, Tien Giang Province.
- A man robbed a bank using a homemade firearm in Trung An, My Tho, Tien Giang Province.

Police detected cases where traffickers disassemble the firearms and send them via post to customers, who then reassemble them. A Dong Thap Provincial Police official said users often purchase such weapons online or in parts and assemble them themselves. Provincial police will initiate a public amnesty campaign for civilians to surrender such weapons. a Tra Vinh police official said in 10 months in 2023, they detected 11 weapons violations involving 52 suspects and seized 13 "military" guns, 4 air guns, 7 homemade guns, and 925 rounds of assorted ammunition.
Weapons: 400 toy guns, intended for conversion (craft handguns)
Actors: Criminal individual

Title: Border guards seize pistols from man at Cambodia border crossing in Long An
Location: My Quy Tay Border Guard Post, Duc Hue District, Long An

Title: Resident arranges voluntary surrender of online-purchased gun in Thua Thien-Hue

Title: Police Seize 82 Firearms From Arms Manufacturing and Ammunition Supply Network in Rach Gia
Location: Vinh Thanh Van, Rach Gia, Kien Giang
Description:
Police seized "many tools and equipment for making guns" after they arrested Duong Minh Tuan for possessing methamphetamines. Tuan confessed that he had gone online to study how to make firearms and had ordered ZP-5 guns, air guns, and other components. He then hired Tran Van Nang in Rach Gia to cut and lathe 6 sets of copper pipes for gun barrels between May and August 2022. The suspect then assembled 15 firearms and ordered 30 bullets for VND 74,000/bullet before selling nine firearms to 10 suspects for VND 1-5.5 million.

Tuan purchased ammunition and pre-converted firearms from Cao Van Hoai and his wife Vo Ngoc Tram, who then resold the finished weapons over Zalo and Facebook (Hoai admitted selling 71 guns to 62 buyers nationwide for VND 7-12 million apiece). From the beginning of 2022 until August 24, 2022, through the express delivery service of the bus companies, Hoai and Tram sourced about 400 guns of various types, about 1,300 rubber bullets, sports bullets, about 1,300 CO2 gas cylinders from Vu Thi Diep in Ho Chi Minh City (see VNM.2022.10.16.001). Police seized 82 guns and 341 rounds of ammunition from this network.

82 converted handguns (craft handguns)
341 rounds of ammunition
Actors: Criminal organization (manufacturing/ammunition supply network); Police

Title: Police Dismantle Gun-Equipped Robbery Gang Targeting Women in Jewelry in HCMC and Mekong Delta

Title: Two business directors jailed after AK, CZ75 pistol 'stand-off' over debt dispute in Ha Tinh
Location: Huong Khe Town, Huong Khe District, Ha Tinh
Description:
Police recovered one Type 81-1 assault rifle and one CZ75 pistol from Le Xuan Giap and Tran Phat Dat, two local business directors, after Giap fired six rounds from the rifle skyward outside his home to intimidate Dat during a dispute over unpaid business debts in Huong Khe Town, Huong Khe District, Ha Tinh, on 19 August 2022; Dat had arrived at Giap's home carrying the loaded CZ75 to confront him before the two men reconciled and went inside together.

The pair enlisted an acquaintance, Ho Hong Quang, to help hide the weapons — Giap buried the rifle in his garden and buried the ammunition separately, while Quang threw the pistol into a nearby reservoir — but investigators recovered both weapons after a week-long inquiry that included a mine-clearance unit dredging the reservoir. All three men were arrested and charged with illegal possession and use of a military-pattern firearm; Giap, who has prior convictions for murder and illegal firearms possession, was additionally investigated for making death threats.

Title: Man arrested for firing three-barrel craft handgun at rival's home in Ninh Thuan
Location: Bao An Ward, Phan Rang - Thap Cham City, Ninh Thuan
Description: Police seized a revolver when they arrested Tran Ngoc Sang at his residence in Bao An Ward, Phan Rang - Thap Cham City, Ninh Thuan on 15 August 2022. Title: Four men charged over handgun resale chain in Tra Vinh
Location: Khom 6, Cang Long Town, Cang Long District, Tra Vinh
Description:
Police seized a converted handgun and five rounds of ammunition from Nguyen Trong Tinh as he attempted to return it to seller Tran Hu Thang in Khom 6, Cang Long Town, Cang Long District, Tra Vinh, around 9 August 2022. In January 2022, Bui Thanh Tha arranged for Tinh to collect the gun and five rounds and sell them to Thang for VND 3.5 million. In May 2022, Thang resold the weapon to Le Van Giang for VND 5 million, but after finding the gun did not fire properly, Giang asked Tinh to return it to Thang for a refund, promising Tinh VND 2 million for the errand. Tinh was stopped and searched by police while carrying the gun.

Police charged and detained Tinh for illegal possession and Thang for illegal trading of a military-grade weapon on 9 August 2022; Tha, who had fled to Tan Phu Ward, District 7, Ho Chi Minh City, was tracked down and arrested there, with charges and detention formalized on 10 November 2022, while Giang was also charged with illegal possession. Title: Authorities Charge Ringleader of 600+ Firearm Trafficking Network Spanning Six Provinces in Nha Trang
Location: Nha Trang, Khanh Hoa (network spanning Kien Giang, An Giang, Ca Mau, Binh Duong, HCMC)
Description:
The authorities charged 17 members of a suspected arms trafficking ring active in Nha Trang, Khánh Hòa Province; Rạch Giá City, Kien Giang Province;  An Giang Province; Ca Mau Province; Binh Duong Province; and Ho Chi Minh City. The suspected ring is thought to have trafficked more than 600 firearms. Police arrested the suspects in August 2022, along with a related network (see VNM.2022.08.22.001).

The case originated with a Kien Giang-led investigation opened August 2022 that was prompted by a rise in armed disputes and protection rackets in Rach Gia and other Kien Giang districts in late 2021/early 2022. Vu Thi Diep, the alleged head of the distribution network, had first been charged in 2019 for illegal weapons sales but was allowed a suspended sentence because she was raising a young child. Despite this, she "continued to make connections to sell weapons from Cambodia to Vietnam." Police identified Diep as a principal supplier of a separate sale of 100 Chinese-made bladed weapons in My Tho, Tien Giang in September 2022 that linked to the broader network.

In August 2022, police arrested one of the syndicate members, Duong Minh Tuan, for storing meth in a motel room in Rạch Giá City, Kien Giang Province (see VNM.2022.08.22.001). Police also found tools for manufacturing/altering firearms. A local couple, Cao Van Hoai and Vo Ngoc Tram, supplied preconverted firearms and sold the finished products over social media. Diep allegedly supplied the couple with 400 guns, 1,300 rubber bullets and 1,300 pressurized gas canisters between early 2022 and October 17 2022.

On 13 October, Diep directed Dang Van Tinh (in Di An, Binh Duong) to ship three boxes of 63 guns via a Mien Dong bus-station freight service to "Huan" in Nha Trang. Tinh was arrested on 16 October with two BB guns, a folding knife, and a phone. The recipients — brothers Dang Quoc Huan and Dang Quoc Anh, from Phu Yen, living together in Nha Trang — admitted receiving regular shipments from Diep to distribute as her regional dealers across central Vietnam, storing them at a warehouse on Le Hong Phong street, Phuoc Long ward, Nha Trang. Police seized 134 M1911-pattern pistols, 64 revolvers, and 31 rubber-bullet/tear-gas guns (229 total, all presumably converted/convertible firearms), plus 455 pressurized gas canisters and 6 kilograms of steel BB pellets. The network reportedly used non-registered promotional SIM cards and bank accounts purchased online to evade tracking. Police arrested Diep along with three of her accomplices in HCMC, Binh Duong, and Khánh Hòa. Photographs showed dozens of revolvers and pistols.
Weapons: 229 unspecified firearms, images show mix of revolvers and pistols (presumably converted, i.e. craft handguns)
Actors: Criminal organization (arms trafficking ring, led by Vu Thi Diep); Police

Title: Residents surrender CKC rifle and homemade gun in Phu Yen amnesty campaign
Location: Xuan Quang 2 Commune, Dong Xuan District, Phu Yen
Description: Residents Tran Van Dun and Nguyen Hai Son voluntarily surrendered an SKS rifle, 85 rounds of ammunition, and a homemade gun they said they had found by chance to police in Xuan Quang 2 Commune, Dong Xuan District, Phu Yen in early August 2022. Title: Police seize three firearms and ammunition from drug dealer's home in Vinh Long

Title: Police Dismantle Major Arms Trafficking Network Selling Converted Airsoft Pistols in Ho Chi Minh City
Location: Pham Huu Lau Street, Phuoc Kieng, Nha Be, HCMC
Description:
Police seized 33 pistols, three revolvers, and dozens of ammunition boxes among other weapons when they arrested members of a suspected arms trafficking network in HCMC. A police patrol first conducted a vehicle inspection on Trang Tu Street (Ward 2, District 6), discovering and seizing one revolver and 10 rounds of ammunition. The suspect confessed he was hired to deliver the weapons on behalf of Tran Duy Khanh (see event dated 10/26/2023), a personal friend. The individual said he was paid VND 100,000 for each delivery. 

Police raided Khanh's internet shop and residence on Pham Huu Lau Street, seizing 33 pistols, 2 revolvers, and dozens of ammunition boxes (possibly magazines). Khanh was reportedly an arms enthusiast who learned how to assemble weapons online and began sourcing supplies to sell weapons online and to acquaintances. Khanh sold weapons to individuals on Facebook, Zalo, TikTok, etc. He apparently bought supplies in bulk batches and sold to customers outside of his local area, in order to protect himself. 

A video showed dozens of Colt M1911 pistols (likely converted airsoft guns), one revolver, and one air rifle.

Title: Off-duty policeman kills five with Cambodia-sourced AK rifle in Ho Chi Minh City shooting spree
Location: Tan Hiep Commune, Hoc Mon District, HCMC
Description:
Police seized a Type 56-1 assault rifle and 9 rounds of ammunition when they killed Le Quoc Tuan, a serving District 11 police officer, during stand-off in Tan Hiep Commune, Hoc Mon District, Ho Chi Minh City on 13 February 2020. The incident was the culmination of a two-week manhunt for Tuan, who shot and killed five people and wounded four at a gambling den in Hamlet 5, Tan Thanh Dong Commune, Cu Chi District, Ho Chi Minh City on 29 January.

The initial shooting began after Tuan lost money in a dice game. He retrieved the rifle, returned to the game, and opened fire on the gamblers (killing four and wounding two), before stealing a motorbike and roughly VND 802 million. During his flight, he stole another motorbike from a couple, fired on a passing car (wounding two), and killed a fifth victim as he stole another motorbike. He went into hiding with the help of relatives and acquaintances.

Hundreds of police officers besieged his hideout at an associate's home in Tan Hiep Commune, Hoc Mon District on 13 February. Police killed Tuan after he opened fire on them and seized his weapons. They traced the items, along with a K54 pistol, a K59 pistol, and two hand grenades to Pham Thanh Tam, who acquired them in Cambodia in 2018-2019 and distributed them to Tuan and other associates for safekeeping; one recipient later sold the K59 and its ammunition to Nguyen Van Vui, who surrendered it to police, while another buried the K54 by throwing it into a pond after growing fearful of detection.

Ho Chi Minh City People's Court tried Tuan (posthumously, with the case against him closed) and 19 co-defendants for murder, robbery, illegal weapons trafficking/possession, harboring stolen property, and concealing a criminal.

Police seized six guns, 10 5.56mm bullets, 731 bullets used for support tools and sports weapons (presumably pellets), along with many gun manufacturing tools when they raided the workshop of a suspected gun manufacturer. The packages contained gun parts and ammunition ordered off of social media networks since October 2019, namely from accounts with Chinese names on Facebook (Hung Chien) and Zalo (Hung Dan).

The suspect had ordered 210 rounds of ammunition and parts for assembling firearms on at least four occassions, using them to produce three firearms and six "support" firearms (likely pellet guns/air rifles). The suspect used social media networks to trade items with individuals in Lang Son, Dak Lak, and HCMC. He also received orders to repair guns for between VND 500,000 and VND 5 million and orders to make four "military" firearms. The suspect had a previous conviction for illegally transporting firearms. Images showed one revolver, at least seven pistols and pistol frames, several magazines, about 120 of rounds of ammunition, and gun manufacturing equipment.
Weapons:
1 revolver
7 pistols
10 rounds of ammunition
Actors: Criminal organization (gun manufacturing/selling network); Police

Title: Police seize AR-15 assault rifle from poacher in Phu Yen
Location: Long Ha Hamlet, La Hai Town, Dong Xuan District, Phu Yen
Description:
Police seized a disassembled AR-15 assult rifle and 17 rounds of ammunition from Vo Dam (born 1969) as he returned from a hunting trip at Long Ha Hamlet, La Hai Town, Dong Xuan District, Phu Yen on 3 January 2020. Dam had found the rifle along with 40 rounds of ammunition while operating an excavator on a land-leveling job in Son Dinh Commune, Son Hoa District in April 2019. He discarded roughly 20 corroded rounds but hid the rifle and remaining ammunition at home for hunting.

On 3 January, Dam packed the items and rode by motorbike toward Xuan Son Nam and Xuan Son Bac communes in Dong Xuan District to hunt. Around 2am the next morning, as Dam returned through Long Ha Hamlet with the disassembled rifle and ammunition, a Dong Xuan District police patrol stopped and searched him, seizing the weapon; he was subsequently prosecuted for illegal possession and use of a military-grade weapon.
Weapons:
1 AR-15 assault rifle
17 rounds of 5.56mm ammunition
Actors: Criminal Individual (Vo Dam, born 1969); Police (Dong Xuan District Police patrol).

Title: Police Seize Pistol and Revolver From Laotian Drug Trafficking Ring Near Laos Border in Ha Tinh
Location: National Highway 8A - Cau Treo, Huong Son District, Ha Tinh
Description: Police seized two handguns and 50 rounds of ammunition when they arrested six Laotian nationals in two separate busts related to drug trafficking. The first took place when police arrested two suspected drug traffickers transporting heroine and methamphetamine along National Highway 8A. Police later arrested four accomplices tasked with scouting the rout and allerting those transporting the contraband of risks along the route. The group was part of a drug trafficking ring that moved drugs from Laos into Vietnam via the Cau Treo border crossing into Huong Son District, Ha Tinh Province.

1 pistol

50 rounds of ammunition

Location: Ea Mta A, Ea Bhok, Cu Kuin, Dak Lak
Description: A man used an AK pattern assault rifle and 27 rounds of ammunition in an attempted murder-suicide with his partner during a fight. After seriously wounding his partner and attempting to commit suicide, the suspect was hospitalized. He subsequently escaped and attempted to flee to the north of the country with an accomplice before being arrested in Da Nang.

Title: Former Toll Booth Guards Rob Employer at Gunpoint in Dong Nai
Location: Dau Giay toll booth, HCMC-Long Thanh-Dau Giay expressway, Dong Nai
Description: Police recovered a pistol that two suspected toll booth robbers attempted to burn shortly after their heist in which the stole VND 2.22 billion (USD 96,000). Both suspects formerly worked as guards at the state enterprise that managed the toll booth but were fired for gambling and poor performance. Weapons: 1 pistol

Title: Police kill two drug kingpins, seize cache of 49 firearms and 17 grenades in Son La
Location: Ta De Hamlet, Long Luong Commune, Van Ho District, Son La
Description:
Police seized a cache of 49 military-grade firearms (including AK-pattern assault rifles, carbines, and K54 and K59 pistols), 17 hand grenades, and roughly 7,000 rounds of ammunition when they raided a fortified compound used by drug traffickers in Ta De Hamlet, Long Luong Commune, Van Ho District, Son La between 26-30 June 2018. Personnel killed drug-trafficking fugitives Nguyen Thanh Tuan (born approximately 1983) and Nguyen Van Thuan, alias "Thuan chot"/"Thuan chuot" (born approximately 1984), and two other suspects during the operation.

Tuan and Thuan had been fugitives since a 2015 case involving 490 kg of heroin smuggled in gas cylinders, and had built a compound with surveillance cameras, barbed wire, and a bunker stocked with fuel and gas canisters to resist capture. Hundreds of security personnel, backed by armored vehicles, besieged the site. When the suspects opened fire, police killed Tuan, Thuan, and two other suspects and arrested three more.

The subsequent search recovered 38 firearms, 8 grenades, and over 6,000 rounds at Tuan's house, and 4 firearms, 3 grenades, and over 400 rounds at Thuan's house. Images showed one M16A1 assault rifle, two Type 81-1 assault rifles, one QBZ-95B assault rifle, one AMD-65 assault rifle, one AK-pattern assault rifle, one M1 carbine rifle, two bolt action rifles, four shotguns, eight M26 hand grenades, five pistols, and thousands of rounds of loose and packaged ammunition.
